name: Gurugram Tech Employee Unpaid Salary & Relieving Letter Withheld
raw_input: I worked as a frontend developer at an IT consultancy firm in Cyber City, Gurugram for 18 months at Rs 70,000/month. I submitted my resignation on 1st August 2024 and completed my full 60-day notice period till 30th September 2024. All project handovers and company assets (MacBook, ID card) were handed over and I received an asset clearance certificate from IT. My August salary was delayed, and my September salary plus 15 days encashable leave (total Rs 1,65,000) has not been paid. It has been 50 days since my last working day. Whenever I email HR, they say 'finance team is facing client payment delays'. More importantly, they are withholding my Relieving Letter and Experience Certificate. My new employer is threatening to cancel my job offer if I don't submit my relieving letter by end of this week. I have my appointment letter, resignation acceptance email, and signed clearance form.

case_dossier.case_title: Withholding of Final Settlement & Relieving Letter by IT Firm
case_dossier.summary: The complainant completed an 18-month tenure and a 60-day notice period at an IT consultancy in Gurugram, successfully clearing all asset handovers. The employer has withheld the final salary and leave encashment totaling Rs. 1,65,000 for 50 days, along with the essential Relieving Letter and Experience Certificate, threatening the complainant's new job offer.
case_dossier.opposite_party: IT Consultancy Firm, Cyber City, Gurugram (Management / HR)

timeline.event: Complainant worked as a frontend developer at Rs 70,000/month.
Completed 60-day notice period, handed over assets, and received asset clearance certificate.
Salary for August and September plus leave encashment unpaid; HR cites client payment delays; Relieving letter withheld.

evidence_held: Signed asset clearance form / certificate from IT
evidence_needed: Bank statements showing salary credits for previous months to establish salary baseline
Written correspondence / email threads with HR regarding the payment delay
Employment contract / offer letter outlining notice period and leave encashment terms
Written communication from the new employer regarding the threat of offer cancellation
case_dossier.evidence_strength_explanation: Strong documentary proof of employment, resignation acceptance, and formal clearance exists, though written follow-ups regarding the unpaid dues should be formally consolidated.

escalation_check.legal_aid_contact: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: 15100

rights_advice.plain_language_standing: Your dispute regarding unpaid wages and final documents is strictly civil in nature, meaning criminal police complaints are not appropriate here. Under Indian law, your wages must be paid promptly following your departure. You hold strong documentation such as an asset clearance certificate and resignation acceptance to support your claim.

governing_laws.relevance: Mandates that wages of an employee who is removed, dismissed, retrenched, or resigns must be paid within two working days of that event.

governing_laws.act_name: General Legal Principle (Civil vs. Criminal Boundary)
governing_laws.relevance: Establishes that withholding wages or breach of employment terms is a civil matter and not a criminal offense, requiring civil/statutory forum resolution instead of police complaints.

action_options.title: Immediate Pre-Litigation Action
action_options.details: Send a formal written demand email to your former employer citing Section 17(2) of the Code on Wages, 2019, requesting the immediate release of your unpaid wages and relieving documents within two working days.

action_options.title: Statutory Authority / Grievance Portal Filing
action_options.details: Approach the competent labour authority (confirm locally) for formal proceedings and recovery of your unpaid wages. Note: The District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Helpline 15100 provides free legal aid and guidance only; it is never a forum for hearings or proceedings against an employer.

action_options.title: Statutory Forum / Conciliation Petition
action_options.details: If the employer fails to comply with your written demand, file a formal dispute petition before the labour authority for conciliation and recovery of dues.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: Given the complexity involving your new job offer and withholding of relieving documents, consulting a licensed advocate or contacting the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) via helpline 15100 for free legal aid and guidance is recommended.
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self-advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

legal_notice_draft:
**BY SPEED POST WITH ACKNOWLEDGEMENT DUE (AD) / REGISTERED EMAIL**

**To,** 
Management / HR Department 
IT Consultancy Firm 
Cyber City, Gurugram, Haryana 

**From:** 
Frontend Developer (Ex-Employee) 
[Complainant Address / Contact Details] 

**Date:** 09/11/2026 

---

### **SUBJECT: LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE FOR WITHHOLDING OF FINAL SETTLEMENT (RS. 1,65,000), LEAVE ENCASHMENT, AND ESSENTIAL RELIEVING DOCUMENTS**

Sir/Madam,

Under instructions from my client, the undersigned submits as under:

1. That my client was employed with your IT consultancy firm situated at Cyber City, Gurugram, as a Frontend Developer for an[unverified reference removed]-month tenure prior to August 2024, drawing a monthly salary of Rs. 70,000/-.
2. That on 1st August 2024, my client formally submitted their resignation from the said position.
3. That my client successfully completed their 60-day notice period ending on 30th September 2024, during which all company assets were duly handed over, and my client received the official signed asset clearance form/certificate from the IT department.
4. That despite the successful completion of the notice period and asset handover, your office has withheld my client's final salary for August and September alongside leave encashment, totaling Rs. 1,65,000/-, for the past 50 days (post-30th September 2024), citing internal client payment delays as an arbitrary excuse.
5. That your office has further withheld my client’s essential Relieving Letter and Experience Certificate, which has severely jeopardized my client's new employment offer and career prospects.

#### **VIOLATION OF STATUTORY PROVISIONS:**
* **Section 17(2) of the Code on Wages, 2019:** Mandates that wages of an employee who resigns must be paid within two working days of their departure. Your failure to clear my client's dues for over 50 days is a blatant violation of statutory wage mandates.
* **General Legal Principle:** Withholding lawful earnings and mandatory exit documents constitutes a civil breach of employment terms. *(Note: For free legal aid and guidance regarding this matter, citizens may reach out to the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: 15100).*

---

#### **DEMAND FOR RECTIFICATION:**

You are hereby called upon to clear and disburse the total withheld amount of **Rs. 1,65,000/-** (representing unpaid salary and leave encashment) and issue the mandatory **Relieving Letter and Experience Certificate** to my client within a strict **15-day window** from the receipt of this notice.

Failure to comply within the stipulated 15-day rectification window will compel my client to initiate formal legal proceedings by filing a dispute petition and seeking recovery before **the competent labour authority (confirm locally)**, alongside pursuing all available remedies under civil law for damages and mental harassment, entirely at your risk as to costs and consequences.

---

**Signature:**

________________________________________ 
**Frontend Developer (Ex-Employee)** 
[Date: 09/11/2026] 

---

#### **ANNEXURE INVENTORY (Documents Held by Complainant):**
1. Appointment letter
2. Resignation acceptance email
3. Signed asset clearance form / certificate from IT

sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Under employment laws, full and final dues must be cleared timely and withholding my relieving letter violates my right to livelihood. If my Rs 1,65,000 and relieving letter are not issued within 3 days, I will file a formal complaint with the District Labor Commissioner.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Arre yaar, yeh sab District Labor Commissioner aur right to livelihood ki dhamkiyan humein mat do! Company policy saaf kehti hai ki exit formalities aur internal audit clear hone ke baad hi FNF process hota hai. Thoda patience rakho, HR team review kar rahi hai. Aise 3 din ki deadline dene se kaam thodi fast ho jayega, agreement padho apna!

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: You firmly invoked statutory rights, exact dues (Rs. 1,65,000), a strict timeline, and threatened a specific legal authority (District Labor Commissioner).
coach_evaluation.what_to_improve: You didn't mention specific sections of the Industrial Disputes Act, Shops & Establishment Act, or the exact date your notice period ended and asset clearance was acknowledged via email.
coach_evaluation.suggested_next_counter: Cite our email confirmation dated [Date] where asset handover was accepted, and remind them that withholding FNF beyond standard statutory timelines attracts legal escalation under the relevant Shops and Establishment Act.
